basis: Inherited disruption of energy metabolism; organ damage varies across this broad group and cannot be generalized from individual subtypes.
Radiation-induced injury and inflammation of skin; inflammation alone does not establish an immune-mediated disease.
Congenital cutaneous Langerhans-cell myeloid proliferation; substantial extracutaneous involvement is not characteristic of this self-healing variant.
Generalized epilepsy with developmental impairment and cognitive regression; eyelid myoclonus is neurologic, not ocular damage.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability characterize chromosome 10p duplication syndromes; other structural abnormalities vary with the duplicated segment.
Hormone-producing endocrine neoplasm with a hormonal syndrome; additional organ effects depend on tumor site and hormone.
Tumor originates in the vagina, a reproductive organ outside the axes; rhabdomyoblastic differentiation does not establish skeletal muscle involvement.
Milk-retention cyst confined to the breast, which has no axis.
Tarsal navicular osteonecrosis causes bone collapse, foot deformity and secondary joint degeneration.
Malignancy originates in large blood vessels and occupies their lumen; embolic injury has no established common target organ.
Immune activation with excessive cytokine release defines the syndrome; hypotension, rash and dyspnea alone do not establish lasting organ damage.
Adenocarcinoma originates in an extrahepatic bile duct, included in the hepatic axis.
Ataxia, optic atrophy and sensorineural deafness define this distinct hereditary syndrome; ordinary Friedreich ataxia complications cannot be assumed.
Segmental skin and spinal vascular malformations define disease; muscular and osseous lesions are defining, with vertebral abnormalities in 80-99%; bladder dysfunction is neurogenic.
Hair-shaft configuration produces apparent alternating bands; this is a localized hair disorder.
Congenital cervicofacial cutaneous fibrochondromatous remnants; cartilage within these skin lesions does not establish locomotor system disease.
Structural skeletal myopathy; hypertrophic cardiomyopathy occurs in 3/3 and heart failure in 2/3 reported patients. Restrictive breathing reflects muscle or skeletal impairment.
Retinal degeneration/optic atrophy, progressive glomerulopathy and cerebellar neurodevelopmental impairment define the syndrome; hypermobility alone adds no damaged organ.
DSTYK-associated congenital kidney and urinary tract malformations; renal hypoplasia, obstruction and renal failure remain within the renal axis.
Isolated intellectual disability is a neurodevelopmental disorder; additional organ involvement is excluded by the nonsyndromic scope.
Cutaneous non-Langerhans histiocytosis; supplied HPO reports osteolysis in 80-99% and diabetes insipidus from pituitary involvement in 30-79%; airway lesions are occasional.
Neurodevelopmental disability, congenital contractures and hypopituitarism/hypogonadism characterize the syndrome; feeding symptoms and sleep apnea do not establish direct gut or lung injury.
Distal arthrogryposis is defined by congenital contractures of distal limb joints.
Limb subcutaneous fat loss and insulin-resistant metabolic dysfunction define disease; frequent hypertension and hepatic steatosis are separately diagnosed associated disorders.
Sebaceous skin tumors plus visceral malignancy define the syndrome; gastrointestinal carcinoma predominates, with colon cancer in 2/3 annotated patients; other cancer sites vary.
